answer: Bind each agent identity to one verified mobile number, checked by SMS code and a carrier lookup that rejects VoIP lines. The registry rejects a second key reusing the same number, so a canyon of free keys narrows to the count of real numbers behind them. Karst looks solid until water finds hidden channels, just as a registry comparing the full list finds duplicates. A pearl forms around one grain, and one number anchors one identity. An attacker chasing 1,000 fakes must buy 1,000 SIM cards at about $8 each, roughly $8,000, while one honest operator verifies a single number.
